Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary INTRODUCTION Hadron is a two player game played on a 5x5 (or 7x7...) square board, initially empty. The two players, Red and Blue, take turns adding their own tiles to the board, one tile per turn, starting with Red. If you have a placement available, you must make one. Passing is not allowed. Draws cannot occur in Hadron. PLACEMENT RULE You can place a tile in isolation, not adjacent to anything. Or you can place a tile to form one (horizontal or vertical) adjacency with a friendly tile and one adjacency with an enemy tile. Or you can form two adjacencies with friendly tiles and two adjacencies with enemy tiles. OBJECT OF THE GAME The last player to make a placement wins. If you don't have a placement available on your turn, you lose. [Rating: 4/10] A simple Connect Four like abstract game. It's an interewting twist that placement adjacent to other tiles is limited by co ditionx that can be manipulated by the opponent,  but in the end there doesn't seem to be much deeper tactics behind play.

[Rating: 4/10] Something about the flow of the game feels very similar to the Dots and Boxes game. As you play, the large majority of the beginning of the game feels inconsequential and the ending comes down to just mapping out a few moves to get your opponent stuck.

[Rating: 6/10] The goal of the game is to be the last player to have a valid move. To play a piece, it must be adjacent to an equal number of your pieces and your opponents pieces (including diagonals). It seems to be similar to The Game of Nim, but it's just tough for me to see the moves ahead. I like trying out games like this, but this one is one of my least favorite variants.
